svg.title: Scalar propagation through a compact cap
svg.desc: Real slice with T=1, delta=1/2, epsilon=1, R=9/4 and eta=1/2. The compact triangular cap lies strictly inside its Cauchy diamond; its Euclidean thickening intersected with that diamond is the actual open solution domain. Cap restriction and a finite support-test shift give the forward coherent analytic microsupport inclusion.
svg.text: Scalar propagation through a compact cap
SCP.7–SCP.20 · actual Cauchy domains, restriction maps and finite degree bounds
1. A real slice of the complex domain
Both imaginary coordinates are zero. Coordinate units have the same scale.

Z = (K + B½) ∩ D
Dashed boundaries of D and Z are excluded; K and its bottom face L are compact.
2. The actual restriction is a quasi-isomorphism
RΓ(K; [O →ᴾ O]) → RΓ(L; [O →ᴾ O])
P is surjective on both holomorphic germ spaces. Its homogeneous kernels agree.
The bottom germs retain all normal derivatives. The unique Cauchy solution lives on Z.
SCP.1–SCP.16; the compact-cap criterion then supplies every nearby real C¹ test.
3. A finite scalar-to-system argument
B = 3n + 1, r = B + 1; all support tests of coherent systems lie in [0, B].
T Sol(N) ≅ T Sol(Kᵣ)[−r]
The two sides have degrees [0, B] and [r, B+r], which are disjoint.
SS(Sol N) ⊆ Char(N)
SCP.17–SCP.22 · coherent analytic systems; no holonomicity assumption.
The reverse inclusion requires its separate solution-evaluation comparison.
For P = ∂ₓ, the germ (t−1)⁻¹ cannot reach the vertex (SCP.31–SCP.32).
